clue.text: Get the French to eat out of a trough?

blocks.note: first meaning: the French verb meaning 'to eat'
second meaning: a feeding box for cattle or horses

explanation.surface: Someone is trying to persuade the French to eat straight out of a pig trough.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half asks for the French word for 'to eat', which is spelt the same as the English word for a feeding trough.
explanation.definitionFit: A manger is the long open box from which farm animals feed, as in the stable at Bethlehem.

clue.text: Australian street play is most disciplined

indicators.note: letters at play move about freely, so the word before is rearranged

explanation.surface: A play set on an Australian street is praised as the most rigorous production around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Street play' looks like a kind of theatre, but 'play' is the signal to rearrange the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Austere means strict and severe in self-control, so the superlative describes the most rigorously controlled.

clue.text: Some climbers not using oxygen try to claim they're an elite

indicators.note: doing without something means part of the following word is left out

blocks.note: the gas, taken as written before being cut down

explanation.surface: Mountaineers who climb without bottled oxygen like to think of themselves as an elite.
explanation.walkthrough: A loose clue: climbers who go without 'OXY' gear leave GEN from oxygen; add TRY to get GENTRY.
explanation.definitionFit: The gentry are the well-born upper class just below the nobility, a privileged social group.

clue.text: Goes up again after abnormal scare ends

indicators.note: something abnormal is out of its usual shape, so the letters of the next word are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone climbs back up once a strange fright is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ends' looks like a verb meaning finishes, but it is simply the word placed after the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To reascend is to climb or rise once more, so a person who reascends goes up a second time.

clue.text: Gets together key security devices

explanation.surface: Someone collects a key along with the locks it opens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' seems to belong with the locks, but here it is a musical key, a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To flock is to gather in a crowd, so people who flock to a place congregate there.

clue.text: Father holds ace: it's staggering

indicators.note: one thing holding another has it inside, so the card goes within the title

blocks.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title

explanation.surface: Dad is holding an ace in a card game, and the result is astonishing.
explanation.walkthrough: A facer is an old word for a blow in the face, and so for a sudden, staggering difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: A facer is a sudden setback or shock that leaves someone reeling, something that staggers them.

clue.text: I pose topless, no less unusual but different

indicators.note: having no 'less' means that string of letters is struck out of the word containing it
unusual means out of the ordinary order, so the remaining letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A model announces that posing topless is just as unusual as anything else, only different.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topless' looks like the daring part of the surface; drop its 'less' to leave TOP, then rearrange with I POSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Opposite can mean contrary or entirely unlike, so it serves for different in the sense of the reverse.

clue.text: Milk I spilt on Persian rug

indicators.note: spilt liquid ends up scattered, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to spilling milk on an expensive Persian carpet.
explanation.definitionFit: A kilim is a flat-woven pileless rug from Iran, Turkey and nearby regions.

clue.text: Three-quarter length stockings on the girl? Glory be!

indicators.note: keeping three quarters of something means the last of its four letters is cut off

blocks.note: hose is an old word for stockings

explanation.surface: A girl wearing knee-length stockings prompts an admiring exclamation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Three-quarter length stockings' reads as a fashion item, but it instructs us to keep three of the four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Hosanna is a shout of praise to God in Christian worship, like the exclamation glory be.

clue.text: A toast to sailors, but not with this drink!

blocks.note: old salts are experienced sailors; the published grid transposes two of its letters

explanation.surface: Raising a glass to the sailors, but advising them not to drink this particular beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: The published grid prints SLATS for SALTS, a transposition. Health salts are fizzy powders dissolved in water as a tonic, hardly what you toast with.
explanation.definitionFit: Health salts are effervescent mineral powders stirred into water and drunk as a laxative tonic.

clue.text: Ice-cold copper first becomes spherical

blocks.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A chilled copper object somehow turns into a ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper first' tells us the metal's symbol comes before the word for ice-cold, even though the clue gives them the other way round.
explanation.definitionFit: Cupolar means shaped like a cupola, a rounded dome, so the setter loosely equates it with spherical.

clue.text: Inhabitant in a lather, initially concerned with the home

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the words just before it

blocks.note: a resident lives in a place

explanation.surface: A householder works themselves into a state about domestic matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a lather' looks like a phrase meaning agitated; only its first letters are used.
explanation.definitionFit: Residential describes areas or matters relating to where people live rather than to business.

clue.text: Frenchman carries my trash around and gets a seasonal greeting

indicators.note: things strewn around are scattered about, so all these letters are shuffled together

explanation.surface: A helpful Frenchman takes out the rubbish and is thanked with festive wishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carries' looks like the verb linking the Frenchman to the trash, but it is part of the material to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Wishing someone a merry Christmas is the standard greeting exchanged during the festive season.

clue.text: Growth that's trimmed by Christmas

blocks.note: surface reading: something growing, like a hedge or a beard, cut back in time for the holiday
setter's reading: a plant decorated with tinsel and baubles in December

explanation.walkthrough: 'Trimmed' suggests cutting, but at Christmas trimmings are decorations, so the growth is dressed up rather than cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A fir or spruce decorated indoors is the centrepiece of Christmas, and it is literally a growing plant.

clue.text: Honour at night, it's said, wears headgear

indicators.note: something said is heard rather than read, so the preceding word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: night-time sounds identical to a mounted warrior's title

explanation.surface: An honour bestowed after dark comes with a ceremonial hat.
explanation.walkthrough: The title-holder 'wears' the head covering, which comes after it in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A knighthood is a rank conferred by the monarch as a mark of distinction, an honour in the British system.

clue.text: Seasonal feeling expressed in a rousing "Hurrah!"

blocks.note: first meaning: the festive mood of Christmas
second meaning: a shout of approval that is a fine one

explanation.surface: Christmas spirit bursts out in a hearty shout of joy.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, a rousing hurrah is simply a hearty shout of approval, which is also the old phrase for festive merriment.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means festive merriment and feasting, as in carols, and literally a fine shout of approval.

clue.text: Modified one basic note for a bow

indicators.note: something modified has been altered, so these letters change their order

explanation.surface: A musician alters one simple note to suit a violin bow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bow' looks like part of a stringed instrument in this musical scene, but it means bending at the waist.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeisance is a gesture of respect such as a deep bend of the body or a curtsy.

clue.text: What hosts of angels were doing on Christmas Eve?

definitions.text: What hosts of angels were doing on Christmas Eve?

blocks.clueFragment: What hosts of angels were doing
blocks.note: surface reading: a question about the angels' activity in the nativity story
setter's reading: the angels sang 'Glory to God in the highest', so their activity is giving praise

explanation.walkthrough: In Luke's gospel the heavenly host appear to the shepherds praising God, so a verb built on their opening word fits.
explanation.definitionFit: Glorying means exulting or rejoicing triumphantly, which matches the heavenly host's song of praise to the shepherds.

clue.text: Agrees to accept seats for audition

blocks.note: a settle is a high-backed wooden bench
kept as written; the setter adds 'audition' as a hint that the phrase is to be heard

explanation.surface: Someone at a casting agrees to make do with the seats offered for the audition.
explanation.walkthrough: A settle is a wooden bench with arms and a high back, common in old pubs and farmhouses.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle for something is to accept it reluctantly as good enough, having hoped for more.

clue.text: Sharp cry

blocks.note: first meaning: having a fine cutting edge
second meaning: to wail in grief for the dead

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it sounds like a shrill shout; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Keen describes a blade with a fine edge, and as a verb means to wail mournfully, as in an Irish lament.

clue.text: Get bearings on where the Magi came from

blocks.note: first meaning: to find one's position or direction
second meaning: the East, as in the carol 'We Three Kings'

explanation.surface: Someone finds their bearings by working out the wise men's starting point.
explanation.walkthrough: The carol begins 'We three kings of Orient are', the old name for the lands of the East.
explanation.definitionFit: To orient yourself is to find your direction, and the Orient is a poetic name for the eastern world.

clue.text: Italian wine made with Lamb's tears?

blocks.note: first meaning: a wine from the slopes of Vesuvius
second meaning: Latin for the tears of Christ, the Lamb of God

explanation.surface: A winemaker claims his Italian vintage is made from the tears of a lamb.
explanation.walkthrough: The published grid starts the answer with A, carried over from its SLATS slip in the crossing entry; the wine's name begins with L. The Lamb is Christ.
explanation.definitionFit: The Campanian wine's Latin name translates as the tears of Christ, whom Christians call the Lamb of God.

clue.text: Edible plant -- four eaten by Guevara

indicators.note: something eaten ends up inside the eater, so the number goes within the name

explanation.surface: The revolutionary Che Guevara munches on four herbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Chives are a small onion-family herb whose slender leaves are used in cooking.

clue.text: An original Christmas present first made you really rich here

indicators.note: first means take the opening letter of each of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A gift on the first Christmas made the recipient wealthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Original' refers to the very first Christmas, when the Magi brought gold, frankincense and myrrh.
explanation.definitionFit: Myrrh, an aromatic resin, was one of the three gifts brought by the wise men to the infant Jesus.

clue.text: Hotter price is wrong

indicators.note: something wrong is out of order, so the letters are rearranged correctly

explanation.surface: A shopper complains that a hotter dish has been mispriced.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'is' belongs to the letters as well as the grammar: PRICE plus IS are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Spicier food has more chilli or pepper, so it tastes hotter on the tongue.

clue.text: Timeless quality of the City of Rome

definitions.text: quality of the City of Rome

blocks.clueFragment: quality of the City of Rome
blocks.note: second meaning: Rome's traditional epithet, the ___ City

explanation.walkthrough: Rome has been called the Eternal City since antiquity.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternal means without beginning or end, existing for all time, and is Rome's classic nickname.

clue.text: Extension rod or pole, for example

blocks.note: first meaning: how far something stretches
second meaning: the rod and pole are old units of linear measure

explanation.surface: A handyman needs an extension rod or a long pole to reach something.
explanation.walkthrough: A rod, pole or perch was an old British measure of five and a half yards, so each is an example of a unit of this.
explanation.definitionFit: Length is the extent of something from end to end, and rods and poles are measures of distance.

clue.text: Cad gets woman sooner

blocks.note: a rat is a contemptible person

explanation.surface: A scoundrel wins over a woman before anyone else can.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sooner' looks like it means earlier in time, but here it is the sense of preference, as in 'I'd sooner stay'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rather expresses preference, as in 'I would rather go', exactly like sooner in that phrase.
